cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Make It Official
cards.instruction: Recruit someone by giving them a title, role, or ceremonial duty that makes participation feel binding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've appointed you Keeper of the Festival Lantern. Hold it upright, please; you're representing us now.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only held it while you tied your shoe.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A useful trial. Keep your hand below the glass while I pin on your badge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I leave it at the ticket desk when I go?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hand it to a person, not a desk. Introduce them as the next Keeper and show them the grip before you release it.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 corrects grip while converting a favor into probation and A5 corrects unattended deposit into ceremonial handover, making expert training bind a new title.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 brief favor becomes A3 useful trial and badge; B4 ticket-desk exit becomes A5 named successor and taught grip.

relationship.evidence: B2 protests scope and B4 offers a practical drop-off, believable attempts to limit an imposed role.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 proposed exit to make B recruit and train the next official Keeper before release.

specificity.evidence: A1 festival lantern and B2 shoe-tying favor establish the inflated assignment.
